findings.where: how_questions_and_answer_keys_are_made_and_checked, STEP 7 ("A program refuses any note of any group that holds an option-letter pattern, the question's sentence, an option's full text, or the words answer, option or correct"). Also leakage_and_fairness_controls item 5, and task_design "WRONG OPTIONS. Built from things named in the passage where possible."
findings.problem: The answer-leak screen cannot work as written, and the draft never says what happens after a hit. Options are built from things named in the passage. Notes also name things in the passage. So notes will hold option text very often. An ordinary note that repeats a plain fact holds the right option of the plain-fact question. If a refused ordinary note is written again (the draft does this for its other note checks), the answer key decides what the rival may say: facts that are answers get removed from the rival's notes. Role notes are sealed before questions exist and cannot be rewritten, so the two sides are treated differently. If a hit drops the passage instead, most passages are lost and the launch floor is missed. Either way the operator would have to pick a rule after seeing which notes are hit. That is a rule change outside the reviewed plan.
findings.evidence: The draft's own examples trip the screen. Example 4, right option: "on the shelf". Example 3, ORD-INFORMED illustration for the same passage: "a new radio plays on the shelf". That ordinary note would be refused. The ROLE note for that passage quotes only the first sentence and would pass. Example 2, second question: options "the fish counter" and "the brass band" sit inside the ROLE note ("The fish counter", "The brass band on the corner barely registered.") and inside the ORD-INFORMED illustration ("put off by the fish counter"). Real data, my count: 6 of the 192 eligible passages hold "answer" or "correct" in their own text (V027, V051, V175, V231, V335, V413). 3 role notes carry the word through the supporting quote (V027, V051, V413). The ORD-INFORMED brief tells the writer to include "plain details", so hits on plain-fact options will be common on the rival's side.
findings.smallest_fix: Rewrite the screen in the plan before any seal. (1) Remove the "option's full text" test, or apply it only to option text that is not in the passage. The passage is in every prompt already. (2) Apply "answer", "option", "correct" as whole words, and not to text copied from the passage. (3) State the consequence: a hit never causes any note to be written again. It drops the passage for every group, by program, with the reason logged. (4) Keep the word-matching score as the check for one option standing out in the notes.

findings.where: guidance_groups, "How length is matched" ("Ordinary notes are written to 90% to 100% of the ROLE word count ... Shorter blocks get the '[Padding: neutral ...]' tail"). Also example_tasks Example 1, first line of GROUP ROLE: "Roles in this passage, as marked by two label teams that agree:", and the QUOTES-ONLY heading "Marked parts of this passage:".
findings.problem: The Notes block is not the same frame for every group. First, length is matched in words when the notes are written but in tokens (the word-pieces the model reads) when they are run. The role note is full of quote marks, ^ signs and colons, so it has more tokens per word than plain prose. Every ordinary note therefore gets a tail of padding and the role note gets almost none. The tail sits right before the question. The role note's own filler (heading and canon lines) sits at the top, far from the question. FILLER against NONE does not measure "useful notes followed by junk". So ROLE could beat the ordinary notes because of the junk tail. QUOTES-ONLY would be more than half padding, so "ROLE beats QUOTES-ONLY" would not be clean either. Second, only ROLE and MIXED open with a claim of authority ("as marked by two label teams that agree"). The ordinary notes have no such line.
findings.evidence: Estimate, not B's tokenizer: counting words plus punctuation marks, role notes come to 1.43 per word and passage prose to 1.18. An ordinary note at 90% to 100% of the role note's words is then 17% to 26% padding on average, about 30 to 44 padding tokens, and never under 12% on any passage. QUOTES-ONLY: 57% padding on average (41% to 73%). The heading plus canon lines are 38% of the role note on average, about 50 words. The draft only promises "Average padding per group is reported".
findings.smallest_fix: (1) Put the padding at the start of the Notes block in every group, not at the tail. Then no group has junk next to the question, and QUOTES-ONLY lines sit where the ROLE lines sit. (2) Set the ordinary writer's word target from a count that includes punctuation marks, so its padding is close to zero. (3) Gate 0 already counts real tokens: add one fixed line, written before the run, that the ROLE-against-ordinary result is not read if either ordinary group's mean padding is above 10% of the block. (4) Use one neutral heading for every group, or none. Remove "as marked by two label teams that agree". No canon line is changed.

findings.where: primary_comparison_and_pass_rules, condition C3 and "ALWAYS PRINTED BESIDE THE CODE". guidance_groups 4 (MIXED) and 7 (QUOTES-ONLY: "No pass rule uses it"). practice_run_and_task_selection Gate 7 ("Secondary blocks are then added only if they fit"). how_questions STEP 3 (anchor check). leakage_and_fairness_controls: "Nobody picks tasks by whether a role note looks helpful."
findings.problem: The pass code can be earned without the role names doing any work. The role note often quotes one sentence and names one thing. The anchor check keeps a question only when the words it turns on are in the role note. Wrong options come from other parts of the passage. So the right option is often the one option the note points at. The ordinary notes restate the whole passage and point at nothing. MIXED does not test this, because it carries the same pointing. On PULL-PUSH it also tags the liked thing as ^3 Negative, which pushes B to a wrong option. So "ROLE beats MIXED" can be true only because wrong tags mislead. The one group that separates role names from pointing is QUOTES-ONLY. It is in no pass rule and the time gate may drop it. If it is dropped, the sentence the draft says is "always printed" cannot be printed.
findings.evidence: My counts on the 156 final passages: 69 role notes quote exactly one passage sentence. 44 hold exactly one entry besides ^1. 128 quote at most half of the passage's sentences. By type: FORMED 22 of 37, PARTS 17 of 29, HABIT 16 of 29 quote one sentence. PULL-PUSH, all 54 passages: 28 have both ^2 and ^3 agreed, so the swap points at a named wrong option; 26 have only one of them, so the swap gives the right thing the opposite tag. The draft says it itself: "ROLE can beat MIXED only because wrong tags mislead B." The anchor check is a rule that keeps tasks by what the role note contains, which contradicts the control sentence quoted above.
findings.smallest_fix: (1) Move QUOTES-ONLY into the must-run block and count it in Gate 7. It adds at most 312 calls. (2) Do not let the code's name say more than was shown. Give ROLE_HELP_BEATS_STRONGEST_ORDINARY_HELP only when ROLE also beats QUOTES-ONLY. If all else holds but that does not, print a separate fixed code, for example POINTING_BEATS_ORDINARY_HELP_ROLE_NAMES_NOT_SHOWN. Question for the owner: does a gain from pointing alone (label plus supporting quote, no role name) count as enough reason to build the reader? (3) Print the ROLE-against-ordinary difference again on the fixed sub-view where the word-matching rule does not pick the right option under ROLE. (4) Print, for both ordinary groups, the share of kept questions whose anchor words appear in that group's note, and correct the control sentence.

The pass margin is 5 points. A reply such as {"answer": "C. the smell of damp rope"} is scored WRONG, not FORMAT_FAIL, so it does not even count toward the 25% line. Role notes are full of quoted strings. Ordinary notes are prose and end in padding. Either may change how B writes its reply. This can go for the role notes or against them.
findings.evidence: C:/Users/wakil/OneDrive/Desktop/tksCAS/cas_only_reasoner/CASALESCENCE_NOETICS_v0_1/tools/scorer_v0_1.py lines 36 to 55: a one-key object with a string value is compared with the key, so a dressed letter is WRONG. The draft's near-miss count is an extra view that no rule uses.
findings.smallest_fix: Add one validity rule, written before the run. The scorer stays unchanged. On final role-step tasks, the share of replies that are not exactly one allowed capital letter (FORMAT_FAIL plus CUT_OFF plus dressed letters, by the near-miss count) may differ by at most 5 points between ROLE and each ordinary group. findings.smallest_fix: The reader returns only {'status': code, 'result_sha256': ..., 'result_bytes': ...}. The code must match [A-Z_]{1,80}; anything else becomes the fixed text RESULT_UNREADABLE.
